 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 22.09.2018 passed in MVC.No.5661/2017 by the Additional Small Causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru (SCCH-13), for seeking enhancement of compensation.

 5.
The Tribunal while determining the compensation has not adopted the correct parameters.
Hence, claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation.
6. In the present case, the deceased was aged about 50 years and was working as a driver.
The accident was caused on 06.07.2017, therefore, notional income of the deceased ought to be taken at Rs.11,000/-p.m.
The NC: 2024:KHC:6700 Tribunal has taken the age of the deceased as 49 years as per Ex.P-6-ration card.

The learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurance Company submitted that the age of the deceased is 50 years, therefore submitted 10% income ought to be taken towards 'loss of future prospectus in life'.
7.
The Tribunal has not added income towards 'loss of future prospectus in life'.
Ex .P-6 is the ration card showing the age of deceased as 49 years.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, it is proved that the deceased has not completed age of 49 years.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '13'.
Further 25% of income is to be added towards 'loss of future prospects of life' considering age as 49 years.
8. The claimants are wife and three children of the deceased.
Though, the children are major running the age of 20 to 25 years, but still they are unmarried.
Hence, they are depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, considering the size of the family of the NC: 2024:KHC:6700 deceased, 1/4th of income is to be deduced towards 'personal and living expenses'.

Therefore,
compensation under the head loss of dependency is re-assessed and quantified as under:
Rs.11,000/- + Rs.2,750/- (25% of Rs.11,000/-) = Rs.13,750/-
Rs.13,750/- X 3/4 X 13 X 12 = Rs.16,08,750/-
Thus, appellants/claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,08,750/- towards 'loss of dependency'.
9. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss consortium', which is on the lower side.
There are totally four legal dependants of the deceased.

Hence, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LIMITED VS. NANU RAM & OTHERS1 and NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. VS. PRANAY SETHI,2 (Pranay Sethi's case (supra)), the appellants/claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each with 10% escalation under the head 2018 ACJ 2782 (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC:6700 'loss of consortium' including 'loss of love and affection'.

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.5,77,750/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

14. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part.

The impugned judgment and award dated 22.09.2018 in MVC.No.5661/2017 passed by the Additional Small Causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru (SCCH-13), is modified to the extent that the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.5,77,750/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
